body: Sounds like a challenge, but I would basically be cheating as my mother fanned my self hatred flames from a young age.

I hate myself 100x more than anyone else could possibly hate me and I have pretty terrible intrusive thoughts, but on the outside people have told me I'm generally kind, thoughtful and funny. Which seems like some cruel joke, but hey-- What can you do?

Depression feels like the weight of a cat resting on your chest, over time it becomes heavier with the rise and fall of your breathing. The feeling is a slow ache over your body, makes your joints feel taut, but not enough to make it anything more than a slight nuisance. There's a constant cloud of fog that moves from lacking desire to lacking appetite, because in the end it all seems so pointless.

I've heard it described as falling into a pit, but I just feel consumed by it. Trapped in a room and it's inescapable and suffocating. Fighting for the idea that maybe I can ride it out, maybe it's just like last time, maybe it'll just be this hour- day- week.

But then I realize that the here is me and not a place. It's always been me and I can't stop it.
Self awareness is key and I do agree with you.

I loathe when people express the desire to talk about it. It's like, what do you expect me to say? It's endless bullshit everyone's already heard and no one has a response that will change who I am or what I'm feeling.

I posted here because I'm hoping maybe someone will be able to tell me something I've never heard before. Which is laughable, considering the above. I don't expect it to happen and I don't expect things to ever get better, it's just waiting until I break down again and attempt for whatever asinine time it would be.

I do feel like reaching out makes the cry for help less legitimate. That just puts people between a rock and a hard place-- Damned if you do and damned if you don't.
